feedback: The confession follows the available chain closely: real bottle versus nonexistent projection, poison collected at preview, and later access to the waiting glass. None of those is a decisive new evidentiary premise; the admitted transfer confirms what the false projection story and opportunity already implied. The additional claim that repayment did not prevent exposure of Elle's misuse clarifies continuing motive, although that lingering threat was less explicit before voting. Her final relationship to the fabric gives the confession an emotional cost rather than just reciting guilt. Chip relinquishing workbench keys and Barb protecting caterers also follow their established voices and misconduct. The ending feels earned, with some explanatory repetition of documentary clues but no rescue through a surprise forensic fact.
